docs.title: bridge-island
docs.text:
A Python reference implementation of the bridge/island integration architecture.

A host platform that is certified by someone else and cannot be changed (the Baseline Island) has to work with mission systems that you own and that change on their own schedule (the Unique Island). In this architecture, every exchange between the two islands goes through one mediation layer, the Bridge. When the baseline changes, the change lands in the Bridge's mapping, not in every mission system. This package simulates the pattern on invented platforms, compares it with point-to-point integration, and lets you run, test and extend it.

flowchart LR
    B["Baseline Island<br/>(immutable host platform)"] <-->|published interface only| OIU
    subgraph Bridge
        OIU["OEM Interface Unit<br/>remote terminal"] <--> TM["Translator Module<br/>formats, content, time tags"]
        TM <--> UID["Unique Interface Distributor<br/>bus controller"]
        H["Health monitor"] -.-> TM
        C["Cyber monitor"] -.-> TM
    end
    UID <-->|native protocol| U1["Unique system 1"]
    UID <-->|native protocol| U2["Unique system 2"]
    UID <-->|native protocol| U3["Unique system n"]

Invented content, synthetic numbers

Every platform, message, field, rate and number in this project is invented. Experiment outputs are synthetic and illustrative. This is not flight or medical software, and it is not certified for any use. See Design rationale and limitations.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
From a checkout of the repository, with uv installed:

uv sync --all-groups
uv run bridge-island demo aviation
uv run bridge-island experiment change-impact --seed 1

The demo runs an invented aviation example on two versions of the baseline interface and then compares what the change costs with point-to-point integration. The second command reproduces the change-impact experiment, with a seeded Monte Carlo mode. Both finish in seconds. Output (abridged):

docs.title: Datum dataclass
docs.text:
One element value with its source time of validity (G3), never delivery time.

An estimated datum (see the Bridge's extrapolate rate policy) is a prediction, not a measurement. Its source_time is the time the estimate is valid for, and basis_time is the time of the last real sample it was predicted from. Its age is measured from the basis, so an estimate can never make old information look fresh.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Datum:
    """One element value with its *source* time of validity (G3), never delivery time.

    An *estimated* datum (see the Bridge's ``extrapolate`` rate policy) is a prediction, not a
    measurement. Its ``source_time`` is the time the estimate is valid for, and ``basis_time``
    is the time of the last real sample it was predicted from. Its age is measured from the
    basis, so an estimate can never make old information look fresh.
    """

    element: str
    value: Any
    source_time: float
    estimated: bool = False
    basis_time: float | None = None

    def age(self, now: float) -> float:
        basis = (
            self.basis_time if self.estimated and self.basis_time is not None else self.source_time
        )
        return now - basis

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BamDecode(Transform):
    """Binary angular measurement counts to degrees (float)."""

    bits: int = 16

    @property
    def _step(self) -> float:
        return 360.0 / (1 << self.bits)

    def apply(self, value: int) -> float:
        return value * self._step

    def expr(self, x: str) -> str:
        return f"({x} * {self._step!r})"

    def inverse(self) -> Transform:
        return BamEncode(self.bits)

    def output(self, rep: Representation) -> Representation:
        if rep.encoding != f"bam{self.bits}":
            raise TransformError(f"expected encoding bam{self.bits}, got {rep.encoding!r}")
        return replace(rep, encoding="float64", units="deg")

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BamEncode(Transform):
    """Degrees to binary angular measurement counts (rounded, wrapped)."""

    bits: int = 16

    @property
    def _step(self) -> float:
        return 360.0 / (1 << self.bits)

    def apply(self, value: float) -> int:
        return round(value / self._step) % (1 << self.bits)

    def expr(self, x: str) -> str:
        return f"(round({x} / {self._step!r}) % {(1 << self.bits)})"

    def inverse(self) -> Transform:
        return BamDecode(self.bits)

    def output(self, rep: Representation) -> Representation:
        if (rep.encoding, rep.units) != ("float64", "deg"):
            raise TransformError("BAM encoding needs float64 degrees")
        return replace(rep, encoding=f"bam{self.bits}")

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BitUnpack(Transform):
    """Integer word to a dict of named bit fields (least-significant field first)."""

    fields: tuple[tuple[str, int], ...]

    def apply(self, value: int) -> dict[str, int]:
        return {n: (value >> s) & m for n, s, m in _layout(self.fields)}

    def expr(self, x: str) -> str:
        items = ", ".join(f"{n!r}: ({x} >> {s}) & {m}" for n, s, m in _layout(self.fields))
        return "{" + items + "}"

    def inverse(self) -> Transform:
        return BitPack(self.fields)

    def output(self, rep: Representation) -> Representation:
        return replace(rep, encoding="bitfield")

def check_type(value: Any, encoding: str) -> None:
    """Shallow type check of a value against an encoding name."""
    if encoding.startswith(("float",)):
        ok = isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool)
    elif encoding.startswith(("uint", "bam")):
        bits = int("".join(c for c in encoding if c.isdigit()) or 0)
        ok = isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
        ok = ok and (bits == 0 or 0 <= value < 2**bits)
    elif encoding == "bool":
        ok = isinstance(value, bool)
    else:
        ok = True
    if not ok:
        raise MalformedError(f"{value!r} is not a valid {encoding}")

def from_spec(spec: Any) -> Transform:
    """Build a transform from one YAML mapping-spec entry.

    Raises :class:`TransformError`, and nothing else, for anything that is not a permitted,
    well-formed transform.
    """
    if isinstance(spec, str) and spec == "identity":
        return Identity()
    if isinstance(spec, dict) and len(spec) == 1:
        ((kind, arg),) = spec.items()
        builder = _BUILDERS.get(kind) if isinstance(kind, str) else None
        if builder is not None:
            return builder(arg)
    raise TransformError(f"transform not permitted: {spec!r}")

def coefficients(src: str, dst: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Return ``(scale, offset)`` such that ``dst_value = src_value * scale + offset``."""
    if src == dst:
        _lookup(src)
        return 1.0, 0.0
    dim_s, scale_s, off_s = _lookup(src)
    dim_d, scale_d, off_d = _lookup(dst)
    if dim_s != dim_d:
        raise UnitError(f"cannot convert {src!r} ({dim_s}) to {dst!r} ({dim_d})")
    return scale_s / scale_d, (off_s - off_d) / scale_d

class Scheduler:
    """Runs callbacks in simulated-time order. Ties run in scheduling order."""

    def __init__(self, seed: int = 0) -> None:
        self.now = 0.0
        self.rng = random.Random(seed)
        self._queue: list[tuple[float, int, Callable[[], None]]] = []
        self._seq = 0

    def at(self, time: float, fn: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
        time = round(time, 9)  # keeps k * period free of float drift
        if time < self.now:
            raise ValueError(f"cannot schedule at {time} before now={self.now}")
        heapq.heappush(self._queue, (time, self._seq, fn))
        self._seq += 1

    def after(self, delay: float, fn: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
        self.at(self.now + delay, fn)

    def every(self, period: float, fn: Callable[[], None], start: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """Call ``fn`` at ``start + k * period`` for k = 0, 1, 2, ..."""

        def tick(k: int) -> None:
            fn()
            self.at(start + (k + 1) * period, lambda: tick(k + 1))

        self.at(start, lambda: tick(0))

    def run_until(self, end: float) -> None:
        while self._queue and self._queue[0][0] <= end:
            time, _, fn = heapq.heappop(self._queue)
            self.now = time
            fn()
        self.now = max(self.now, end)

class Network:
    """Registry of nodes and the links wired between them."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.islands: dict[str, str] = {}
        self.links: list[Link] = []

    def add(self, member: IslandMember) -> None:
        self.islands[member.name] = member.island

    def connect(self, a: str, b: str, protocol: str) -> None:
        for n in (a, b):
            if n not in self.islands:
                raise KeyError(f"unknown node {n!r}")
        self.links.append(Link(a, b, protocol))

    def bypass_links(self) -> list[Link]:
        """Links that join a baseline node directly to a unique node."""
        return [
            link
            for link in self.links
            if {self.islands[link.a], self.islands[link.b]} == {"baseline", "unique"}
        ]

    def problems(self) -> list[str]:
        """G1 violations: bypass links, and unique nodes with no link to the Bridge."""
        found = [f"bypass link {lk.a} <-> {lk.b}" for lk in self.bypass_links()]
        for name, island in self.islands.items():
            if island != "unique":
                continue
            peers = {lk.b if lk.a == name else lk.a for lk in self.links if name in (lk.a, lk.b)}
            if not any(self.islands[p] == "bridge" for p in peers):
                found.append(f"{name} has no link to the Bridge")
        return found

docs.text:
Generic command/response bus: one bus controller (BC), many remote terminals (RT).

Only the BC starts transfers; an RT can only answer when commanded. The BC runs a cyclic schedule of minor frames, and a major frame is a fixed number of minor frames.

Generic label-word bus: one transmitter broadcasts labelled words to many receivers.

Generic topic-based publish/subscribe bus (Ethernet-style, higher latency).

def every_for(self, rate_hz: float) -> int:
    """Minor frames between transfers for a rate; the rate must divide the minor rate."""
    ratio = self.minor_hz / rate_hz
    if abs(ratio - round(ratio)) > 1e-9 or ratio < 1:
        raise BusError(f"{rate_hz} Hz does not divide the {self.minor_hz} Hz minor frame")
    return round(ratio)

class BaselinePlatform:
    """Emits its published messages at their rates; accepts only its specified inputs.

    The platform is the bus controller of its own bus. Only a Bridge may attach to it
    (G1) unless ``enforce_bridge`` is switched off to model point-to-point integration.
    """

    sched: Scheduler
    interface: BaselineInterface
    sources: Mapping[str, Source]
    name: str = "baseline"
    sample_age_s: float = 0.005
    enforce_bridge: bool = True
    island: str = field(default="baseline", init=False)
    accepted: list[tuple[float, Message]] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
    rejected: list[tuple[float, str]] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
    emitted: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.bus = CommandResponseBus(self.sched)
        self._bc = BusController(self.name)
        self.bus.set_controller(self._bc)
        self._started = False

    def connect(self, rt: RemoteTerminal, owner: IslandMember) -> int:
        """Attach a remote terminal. Returns its bus address."""
        if self.enforce_bridge and owner.island != "bridge":
            raise BypassError(f"{owner.name!r} ({owner.island}) may not attach to the baseline")
        return self.bus.attach(rt)

    def start(self) -> None:
        if self._started:
            return
        self._started = True
        for rt_addr in self.bus.terminals:
            rt = self.bus.terminals[rt_addr]
            for spec in self.interface.published:
                if spec.subaddress not in rt.on_receive:
                    continue  # this terminal does not take that message
                self._bc.transfers.append(
                    Transfer(
                        rt_addr,
                        spec.subaddress,
                        "bc_to_rt",
                        every=self.bus.every_for(spec.rate_hz),
                        provide=lambda spec=spec: self._emit(spec),  # type: ignore[misc]
                    )
                )
            for spec in self.interface.accepted:
                if spec.subaddress not in rt.on_transmit:
                    continue
                self._bc.transfers.append(
                    Transfer(
                        rt_addr,
                        spec.subaddress,
                        "rt_to_bc",
                        every=self.bus.every_for(spec.rate_hz),
                        consume=self._accept,
                    )
                )
        self.bus.start()

    def _emit(self, spec: MessageSpec) -> Message:
        valid_at = round(self.sched.now - self.sample_age_s, 9)
        self.emitted[spec.name] = self.emitted.get(spec.name, 0) + 1
        return Message(spec.name, dict(self.sources[spec.name](valid_at)), valid_at)

    def _accept(self, msg: Message | None) -> None:
        if msg is None:
            return
        now = self.sched.now
        spec = self.interface.accepted_message(msg.spec_name)
        if spec is None:
            self.rejected.append((now, f"{msg.spec_name} is not an accepted input"))
        elif set(msg.values) != {e.name for e in spec.elements}:
            self.rejected.append((now, f"{msg.spec_name} has the wrong fields"))
        else:
            for e in spec.elements:
                v = msg.values[e.name]
                if e.valid_range and not (
                    isinstance(v, (int, float)) and e.valid_range[0] <= v <= e.valid_range[1]
                ):
                    self.rejected.append((now, f"{msg.spec_name}.{e.name}={v!r} out of range"))
                    return
            self.accepted.append((now, msg))

@dataclass
class UniqueSubsystem:
    """A mission system. It reads data age itself: it never trusts delivery time (G3)."""

    sched: Scheduler
    name: str
    protocol: str  # "pubsub" | "command_response" | "label_words"
    needs: tuple[Need, ...]
    outputs: tuple[Output, ...] = ()
    bus_latency_s: float | None = None
    island: str = field(default="unique", init=False)
    received: list[Received] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
    late: list[Received] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
    unavailable: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)
    annunciations: list[tuple[float, str, str]] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
    _uplink: Callable[[Message], None] | None = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)
    _need_by_name: dict[str, Need] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False, repr=False)
    _latest: dict[str, Received] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False, repr=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self._need_by_name = {n.native_name: n for n in self.needs}
        if len(self._need_by_name) != len(self.needs):
            raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: two inputs have the same native name")

    def need(self, native_name: str) -> Need | None:
        return self._need_by_name.get(native_name)

    def on_data(self, native_name: str, datum: Datum) -> None:
        rec = Received(native_name, datum, self.sched.now)
        self.received.append(rec)
        self._latest[native_name] = rec
        need = self.need(native_name)
        if need and rec.age > need.latency_budget_s:
            self.late.append(rec)

    def on_unavailable(self, native_name: str, reason: str) -> None:
        self.unavailable[native_name] = reason

    def on_annunciation(self, kind: str, detail: str) -> None:
        self.annunciations.append((self.sched.now, kind, detail))

    def latest(self, native_name: str) -> Received | None:
        return self._latest.get(native_name)

    def check(self) -> list[str]:
        """Consumer-side checks at the current time: missing, unavailable or stale inputs."""
        issues = []
        for need in self.needs:
            if need.native_name in self.unavailable:
                issues.append(
                    f"{need.native_name}: unavailable ({self.unavailable[need.native_name]})"
                )
                continue
            last = self.latest(need.native_name)
            if last is None:
                issues.append(f"{need.native_name}: no data")
            elif last.datum.age(self.sched.now) > need.stale_after_s:
                issues.append(f"{need.native_name}: stale")
        return issues

    def send(self, message_name: str, values: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Send a message toward the baseline. The Bridge, not the sender, validates it."""
        if self._uplink is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{self.name} is not connected to a Bridge")
        self._uplink(Message(message_name, dict(values), self.sched.now))

docs.title: The Bridge
docs.text:
The Bridge: one object composing the OIU, TM, UID and the two monitors (G6).

Mixed criticality is handled by internal separation, not by spreading the Bridge across several objects: each component sits in its own partition and talks to the others only through callbacks owned by the Bridge, never through direct references.

OEM Interface Unit (OIU): the Bridge part facing the baseline.

It obeys the baseline's published interface exactly and acts as a remote terminal (RT): it can only answer when the baseline's bus controller commands it (G4).

Translator Module (TM): all format, content, protocol-neutral conversion and time tags.

The mapping is a generated module (G5); the TM only calls it. Time tags follow G3: each datum keeps the source time of validity. time_tag="delivery" is the deliberately naive mode used to demonstrate the error.

Unique Interface Distributor (UID): one separate connection per unique system.

Each connection uses that system's own native protocol. Toward the unique side the UID plays the controlling role: bus controller on a command/response bus, sole transmitter on a label-word bus, publisher on a pub/sub bus.

Health monitor: detects stale data and stall-and-resume discontinuities, and annunciates them.

Cyber monitor: enforces which data may cross the Bridge, and in which direction.

def start(self) -> None:
    """Report removed baseline elements to the affected subsystems, and start monitoring."""
    if self.oiu.rt.address is None:
        raise InterfaceMismatch("no baseline is attached: call attach_baseline() first")
    mapped = (
        {s for _, s, _, _ in self.mapping.DOWNLINKS}
        | {s for _, s, _, _ in self.mapping.UNAVAILABLE}
        | {s for s, _, _ in self.mapping.UPLINKS}
    )
    missing = sorted(mapped - set(self.uid.subsystems))
    if missing:  # otherwise the first datum for them would crash the run, much later
        raise InterfaceMismatch(
            f"the mapping refers to subsystems that are not attached: {missing}"
        )
    for ref, sub, native, reason in self.mapping.UNAVAILABLE:
        self.log.add(
            self.sched.now,
            self.name,
            "bridge.unavailable",
            f"{ref} -> {sub}.{native}: {reason}",
        )
        if sub in self.uid.subsystems:
            self.uid.deliver_unavailable(sub, native, reason)
    period = self.health.check_period_s
    self.sched.every(period, self._scan_if_running, start=period)

class OemInterfaceUnit:
    island = "bridge"

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        interface: BaselineInterface,
        sched: Scheduler,
        log: EventLog,
        on_message: Callable[[Message], None],
    ) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.interface = interface
        self.sched = sched
        self.log = log
        self.on_message = on_message
        self.rt = RemoteTerminal(name)
        self.rejected_in = 0
        self.rejected_out = 0
        self._queues: dict[str, deque[Message]] = {}
        for spec in interface.published:
            self.rt.on_receive[spec.subaddress] = self._receiver(spec)
        for spec in interface.accepted:
            self._queues[spec.name] = deque()
            self.rt.on_transmit[spec.subaddress] = self._transmitter(spec)

    def _receiver(self, spec: MessageSpec) -> Callable[[Message], None]:
        names = {e.name for e in spec.elements}

        def receive(msg: Message) -> None:
            if msg.spec_name != spec.name or not set(msg.values) <= names:
                self.rejected_in += 1
                self.log.add(
                    self.sched.now, self.name, "oiu.reject_in", f"{msg.spec_name} not as published"
                )
                return
            self.on_message(msg)

        return receive

    def _transmitter(self, spec: MessageSpec) -> Callable[[], Message | None]:
        queue = self._queues[spec.name]
        return lambda: queue.popleft() if queue else None

    def submit(self, msg: Message) -> bool:
        """Queue a message for the baseline. Only specified accepted messages get through."""
        spec = self.interface.accepted_message(msg.spec_name)
        if spec is None or set(msg.values) != {e.name for e in spec.elements}:
            self.rejected_out += 1
            self.log.add(
                self.sched.now,
                self.name,
                "oiu.reject_out",
                f"{msg.spec_name} not accepted by baseline",
            )
            return False
        self._queues[spec.name].append(msg)
        return True

class TranslatorModule:
    def __init__(
        self,
        mapping: MappingModule,
        sched: Scheduler,
        log: EventLog,
        time_tag: Literal["source", "delivery"] = "source",
    ) -> None:
        self.mapping = mapping
        self.sched = sched
        self.log = log
        self.time_tag = time_tag
        self.identity_count = 0
        self.translated_count = 0
        self.rejected = 0

    def down(self, msg: Message) -> list[Delivery]:
        outs, errors = self.mapping.translate(msg.spec_name, msg.values)
        for ref, why in errors:
            self.rejected += 1
            self.log.add(self.sched.now, "tm", "tm.reject", f"{ref}: {why}")
        tag = msg.source_time if self.time_tag == "source" else self.sched.now
        result = []
        for ref, sub, native, value, identity in outs:
            if identity:
                self.identity_count += 1
            else:
                self.translated_count += 1
            result.append(Delivery(ref, sub, Datum(native, value, tag)))
        return result

    def up(self, sender: str, msg: Message) -> Message:
        """Translate a unique message to a baseline message. Raises TransformError if bad."""
        name, values = self.mapping.translate_up(sender, msg.spec_name, msg.values)
        return Message(name, values, msg.source_time)

class CommandResponsePort:
    """The UID is the bus controller; the subsystem is a remote terminal."""

    def __init__(self, sched: Scheduler, sub: UniqueSubsystem, on_uplink: Uplink) -> None:
        self.bus = CommandResponseBus(sched, latency_s=sub.bus_latency_s or 0.0005)
        bc = BusController("uid")
        rt = RemoteTerminal(sub.name)
        self.bus.set_controller(bc)
        addr = self.bus.attach(rt)
        self.pending: dict[str, Message] = {}
        self.status_queue: deque[Message] = deque()
        self.up_queue: deque[Message] = deque()
        for i, need in enumerate(sub.needs):
            sa, native = i + 1, need.native_name
            bc.transfers.append(
                Transfer(
                    addr,
                    sa,
                    "bc_to_rt",
                    every=self.bus.every_for(min(need.rate_hz, self.bus.minor_hz)),
                    provide=lambda n=native: self.pending.pop(n, None),  # type: ignore[misc]
                )
            )
            rt.on_receive[sa] = lambda m, n=native: sub.on_data(  # type: ignore[misc]
                n,
                Datum(
                    n,
                    m.values["value"],
                    m.source_time,
                    m.values.get("estimated", False),
                    m.values.get("basis_time"),
                ),
            )
        bc.transfers.append(
            Transfer(
                addr,
                _STATUS_SA,
                "bc_to_rt",
                provide=lambda: self.status_queue.popleft() if self.status_queue else None,
            )
        )
        rt.on_receive[_STATUS_SA] = lambda m: _apply_status(sub, m.values["status"])
        rt.on_transmit[_UPLINK_SA] = lambda: self.up_queue.popleft() if self.up_queue else None
        bc.transfers.append(
            Transfer(
                addr,
                _UPLINK_SA,
                "rt_to_bc",
                every=self.bus.every_for(10),
                consume=lambda m: on_uplink(sub.name, m) if m else None,
            )
        )
        sub._uplink = self.up_queue.append
        self.bus.start()

    def send(self, native: str, datum: Datum) -> None:
        values = {
            "value": datum.value,
            "estimated": datum.estimated,
            "basis_time": datum.basis_time,
        }
        self.pending[native] = Message(native, values, datum.source_time)

    def send_status(self, status: Status) -> None:
        self.status_queue.append(Message("status", {"status": status}, 0.0))

class UniqueInterfaceDistributor:
    island = "bridge"

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        sched: Scheduler,
        log: EventLog,
        on_uplink: Uplink,
        rate_policy: str = "cap",
        max_extrapolation_s: float | None = None,
        is_running: Callable[[], bool] = lambda: True,
    ) -> None:
        """``rate_policy`` says what to do when a subsystem can use a higher rate than the
        baseline supplies: ``"cap"`` delivers only real samples, at most at the subsystem's rate;
        ``"extrapolate"`` delivers one item per period of the subsystem's rate: the freshest real
        sample if one arrived, otherwise an *estimate* (linear for floats, hold for other
        encodings), for at most ``max_extrapolation_s`` after the last real sample (default: 1.5
        periods of that input's source, so a dead source is not masked). A source that
        is already as fast as the subsystem needs is handled exactly as with ``"cap"``. Neither
        policy creates information the baseline did not send: both keep the interface working."""
        if rate_policy not in ("cap", "extrapolate"):
            raise ValueError(f"unknown rate policy {rate_policy!r}; use 'cap' or 'extrapolate'")
        self.name = name
        self.sched = sched
        self.log = log
        self.on_uplink = on_uplink
        self.rate_policy = rate_policy
        self.max_extrapolation_s = max_extrapolation_s
        self._is_running = is_running
        self.subsystems: dict[str, UniqueSubsystem] = {}
        self._ports: dict[str, Port] = {}
        self._last_sent: dict[tuple[str, str], float] = {}
        self._history: dict[tuple[str, str], deque[tuple[float, Any]]] = {}
        self._pending: dict[tuple[str, str], Datum] = {}
        self._gridded: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
        self._ticking: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
        self.sent = 0
        self.decimated = 0
        self.estimates = 0

    def connect(self, sub: UniqueSubsystem) -> None:
        if sub.protocol not in _PORTS:
            raise ValueError(f"{sub.name}: unknown native protocol {sub.protocol!r}")
        self.subsystems[sub.name] = sub
        self._ports[sub.name] = _PORTS[sub.protocol](self.sched, sub, self.on_uplink)

    def deliver(self, subsystem: str, datum: Datum) -> bool:
        """Send a datum on the subsystem's native connection, capped at its useful rate."""
        need = self.subsystems[subsystem].need(datum.element)
        if need is None:
            raise KeyError(f"{subsystem} has no input {datum.element!r}")
        key = (subsystem, datum.element)
        history = self._history.setdefault(key, deque(maxlen=2))
        history.append((datum.source_time, datum.value))
        period = 1.0 / need.rate_hz
        slow = len(history) == 2 and history[1][0] - history[0][0] > period * 1.01
        if self.rate_policy == "extrapolate" and slow:
            # The source is slower than the subsystem can use: deliver on the subsystem's own
            # rate grid, one slot per period, carrying the freshest real sample if one has
            # arrived and an estimate otherwise. Real samples wait for their slot.
            self._gridded.add(key)
            self._pending[key] = datum
            if key not in self._ticking:
                self._ticking.add(key)
                self.sched.every(period, lambda: self._tick(key), start=self.sched.now + period)
            return True
        self._gridded.discard(key)
        self._pending.pop(key, None)
        # The cap is measured in *source* time: it limits the rate of the data, not of its
        # arrival. (Measured in arrival time, a message released late after a stall would use up
        # the slot and a fresh one 0.3 s later would be dropped.) If source time goes backwards,
        # for example after a source restart, accept the datum and start counting again.
        last = self._last_sent.get(key)
        if last is not None and 0 <= datum.source_time - last < period - 1e-6:
            self.decimated += 1
            return False
        self._last_sent[key] = datum.source_time
        self._ports[subsystem].send(datum.element, datum)
        self.sent += 1
        return True

    def _tick(self, key: tuple[str, str]) -> None:
        """One slot of the subsystem's rate grid: a real sample if pending, else an estimate."""
        if key not in self._gridded or not self._is_running():
            return
        subsystem, native = key
        pending = self._pending.pop(key, None)
        if pending is not None:
            self._ports[subsystem].send(native, pending)
            self.sent += 1
            return
        need = self.subsystems[subsystem].need(native)
        if need is None:
            return
        history = self._history[key]
        now = self.sched.now
        ok, value = estimate(
            need.representation.encoding,
            need.representation.units,
            list(history),
            now,
            self.max_extrapolation_s,
        )
        if ok:
            self.estimates += 1

        self._ports[subsystem].send_status(("unavailable", native, reason))

    self,
    name: str,
    sched: Scheduler,
    log: EventLog,
    on_uplink: Uplink,
    rate_policy: str = "cap",
    max_extrapolation_s: float | None = None,
    is_running: Callable[[], bool] = lambda: True,

    baseline supplies: ``"cap"`` delivers only real samples, at most at the subsystem's rate;

    encodings), for at most ``max_extrapolation_s`` after the last real sample (default: 1.5
    periods of that input's source, so a dead source is not masked). A source that
    is already as fast as the subsystem needs is handled exactly as with ``"cap"``. Neither
    policy creates information the baseline did not send: both keep the interface working."""

        raise ValueError(f"unknown rate policy {rate_policy!r}; use 'cap' or 'extrapolate'")

def deliver(self, subsystem: str, datum: Datum) -> bool:
    """Send a datum on the subsystem's native connection, capped at its useful rate."""
    need = self.subsystems[subsystem].need(datum.element)
    if need is None:
        raise KeyError(f"{subsystem} has no input {datum.element!r}")
    key = (subsystem, datum.element)
    history = self._history.setdefault(key, deque(maxlen=2))
    history.append((datum.source_time, datum.value))
    period = 1.0 / need.rate_hz
    slow = len(history) == 2 and history[1][0] - history[0][0] > period * 1.01
    if self.rate_policy == "extrapolate" and slow:
        # The source is slower than the subsystem can use: deliver on the subsystem's own
        # rate grid, one slot per period, carrying the freshest real sample if one has
        # arrived and an estimate otherwise. Real samples wait for their slot.
        self._gridded.add(key)
        self._pending[key] = datum
        if key not in self._ticking:
            self._ticking.add(key)
            self.sched.every(period, lambda: self._tick(key), start=self.sched.now + period)
        return True
    self._gridded.discard(key)
    self._pending.pop(key, None)
    # The cap is measured in *source* time: it limits the rate of the data, not of its
    # arrival. (Measured in arrival time, a message released late after a stall would use up
    # the slot and a fresh one 0.3 s later would be dropped.) If source time goes backwards,
    # for example after a source restart, accept the datum and start counting again.
    last = self._last_sent.get(key)
    if last is not None and 0 <= datum.source_time - last < period - 1e-6:
        self.decimated += 1
        return False
    self._last_sent[key] = datum.source_time
    self._ports[subsystem].send(datum.element, datum)
    self.sent += 1
    return True

Returns (True, value) or (False, None) when no estimate should be made. Floats are extrapolated linearly, other encodings (integer codes, enums, booleans) are held. No estimate is made later than limit seconds after the last real sample (default: 1.5 source periods), so a dead source is not masked, nor across what looks like an angle wrapping round, where a straight line would be badly wrong.

def estimate(
    encoding: str,
    units: str,
    history: list[tuple[float, Any]],
    now: float,
    limit: float | None = None,
) -> tuple[bool, Any]:
    """Estimate a value at ``now`` from the last one or two real samples ``(time, value)``.

    Returns ``(True, value)`` or ``(False, None)`` when no estimate should be made. Floats are
    extrapolated linearly, other encodings (integer codes, enums, booleans) are held. No estimate
    is made later than ``limit`` seconds after the last real sample (default: 1.5 source
    periods), so a dead source is not masked, nor across what looks like an angle wrapping
    round, where a straight line would be badly wrong.
    """
    t1, v1 = history[-1]
    if limit is None:
        limit = 1.5 * (t1 - history[0][0]) if len(history) == 2 else 0.0
    if now - t1 > limit:
        return False, None
    if not encoding.startswith("float"):
        return True, v1
    if len(history) < 2 or t1 <= history[0][0]:
        return False, None
    t0, v0 = history[0]
    half_turn = _HALF_TURN.get(units)
    if half_turn is not None and abs(v1 - v0) > half_turn:
        return False, None
    return True, v1 + (v1 - v0) / (t1 - t0) * (now - t1)

class HealthMonitor:
    """``announce(message_name, kind, detail)`` tells the affected unique systems."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        sched: Scheduler,
        log: EventLog,
        interface: BaselineInterface,
        announce: Callable[[str, str, str], None],
        check_period_s: float = 0.1,
        stale_factor: float = 3.0,
        gap_factor: float = 3.0,
    ) -> None:
        self.sched = sched
        self.log = log
        self.interface = interface
        self.announce = announce
        self.check_period_s = check_period_s
        self.stale_factor = stale_factor
        self.gap_factor = gap_factor
        self._last_source: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._last_arrival: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._stale: set[str] = set()
        self._last_scan: float | None = None

    def observe(self, msg: Message) -> None:
        spec = self.interface.published_message(msg.spec_name)
        if spec is None:
            return
        prev = self._last_source.get(msg.spec_name)
        if prev is not None:
            gap = msg.source_time - prev
            if gap > self.gap_factor / spec.rate_hz:
                self._event("discontinuity", msg.spec_name, f"source time jumped {gap:.3f} s")
            elif gap < 0:
                self._event("out_of_order", msg.spec_name, f"source time went back {-gap:.3f} s")
        self._last_source[msg.spec_name] = msg.source_time
        self._last_arrival[msg.spec_name] = self.sched.now
        if msg.spec_name in self._stale:
            self._stale.discard(msg.spec_name)
            self._event("recovered", msg.spec_name, "data flowing again")

    def scan(self) -> None:
        """Periodic check. The Bridge calls it only while running, so a stall leaves a gap."""
        now = self.sched.now
        if self._last_scan is not None and now - self._last_scan > 2 * self.check_period_s:
            self._event(
                "bridge_stall", "bridge", f"no health scan for {now - self._last_scan:.3f} s"
            )
        self._last_scan = now
        for spec in self.interface.published:
            age = now - self._last_arrival.get(spec.name, 0.0)
            if age > self.stale_factor / spec.rate_hz and spec.name not in self._stale:
                self._stale.add(spec.name)
                self._event("stale", spec.name, f"no data for {age:.3f} s")

    def _event(self, kind: str, subject: str, detail: str) -> None:
        self.log.add(self.sched.now, "health", f"health.{kind}", f"{subject}: {detail}")
        self.announce(subject, kind, f"{subject}: {detail}")  # say which message it is about

def generate(spec_path: Path, dic: Dictionary) -> str:
    """The text of the generated module for a spec, or a CodegenError saying what to fix."""
    spec = _read_spec(spec_path)
    if spec["baseline_version"] != dic.interface.version:
        raise CodegenError(
            f"spec is for baseline v{spec['baseline_version']}, "
            f"interface is v{dic.interface.version}"
        )
    parts = _Parts()
    for entry in _entries(spec, "downlinks", ("from", "to")):
        _downlink(entry, dic, parts)
    for sub, needs in dic.needs.items():
        for n in needs:
            if f"{sub}.{n.native_name}" not in parts.covered:
                raise CodegenError(
                    f"{sub}.{n.native_name} is a declared input but has no mapping entry"
                )
    for entry in _entries(spec, "uplinks", ("from", "to")):
        _uplink(entry, dic, parts)
    return _render(spec, spec_path, dic.interface.version, parts)

def load_module(path: Path) -> ModuleType:
    """Import a Python file by path (generated mappings and example worlds)."""
    name = f"_bridge_island_{path.parent.name}_{path.stem}"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise CodegenError(f"cannot load {path}")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module

docs.title: Point-to-point comparison and analysis
docs.text:
Point-to-point (P2P) integration: each unique system wired straight to the baseline.

The conversions are the same ones the Bridge applies. The difference is where they live: inside every subsystem's own adapter, which sits on the baseline bus as its own remote terminal. Nothing validates what a subsystem sends, and a baseline change is felt by every adapter that reads the changed element.

Interface counts for point-to-point (P2P) versus Bridge integration.

n = baseline data elements, m = unique subsystems, E = dependency edges (element, subsystem). This repository counts at the level of data elements. n is not the number of baseline systems or units, so |E| is a count of element-level dependencies; a count taken at the level of systems would be much smaller and is not comparable with these numbers. P2P: |E| interfaces, worst case n * m Bridge: n + m (one per element on the baseline side, one per subsystem) Bridge, consolidated: 1 + m (all baseline elements through one OIU interface)

What a baseline interface change touches, in each architecture.

Counting model (stated assumptions, not measurements): * The unit of counting is the element-level dependency: an edge (baseline data element, subsystem). A count taken at another level, for example baseline systems or units, is a different quantity and is not comparable with these. * Every dependency edge has tests_per_edge conformance tests (default 1), located in whatever component owns the adapter for that edge. Every subsystem also has one acceptance test. The value of tests_per_edge is arbitrary and it alone drives the size of the "tests failing" row; the difference between the architectures in that row does not depend on it (it is the number of P2P subsystems with code changes minus the number of Bridge subsystems with code changes). * P2P: each subsystem owns its own adapter module. A rename, unit, encoding or removal change needs code in every adapter that reads the element. A rate change needs no code but invalidates timing assumptions, so those subsystems are re-verified. * Bridge: the adapters are entries in one mapping, so those changes touch the Translator Module only. A removed element is the exception: the affected subsystem must also handle the "unavailable" report. The Bridge itself is re-verified after any baseline change.

class DirectAdapter:
    """A subsystem's own baseline adapter. ``mapping`` is the generated module it was written
    against, and ``interface`` the baseline version that module targets."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        platform: BaselinePlatform,
        sub: UniqueSubsystem,
        mapping: ModuleType,
        interface: BaselineInterface,
    ) -> None:
        self.sub, self.mapping = sub, mapping
        self.rt = RemoteTerminal(sub.name)
        self.errors: list[tuple[float, str, str]] = []
        self.uplink_queue: deque[Message] = deque()
        self._last_sent: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._refs = {ref for ref, s, _, _ in mapping.DOWNLINKS if s == sub.name}
        for message in {ref.split(".")[0] for ref in self._refs}:
            spec = interface.published_message(message)
            if spec is not None:
                self.rt.on_receive[spec.subaddress] = self._on_message
        for _, s, native, reason in mapping.UNAVAILABLE:
            if s == sub.name:  # the subsystem's own developers had to add this handling
                sub.on_unavailable(native, reason)
        if sub.outputs:
            sub._uplink = self._send
        for spec in interface.accepted:  # every terminal answers the baseline's polls
            self.rt.on_transmit[spec.subaddress] = self._next_uplink
        platform.connect(self.rt, owner=sub)

    def _on_message(self, msg: Message) -> None:
        now = self.sub.sched.now
        outs, errors = self.mapping.translate(msg.spec_name, msg.values)
        for ref, why in errors:
            if ref in self._refs:
                self.errors.append((now, ref, why))
        for _, s, native, value, _ in outs:
            need = self.sub.need(native)
            if s != self.sub.name or need is None:
                continue
            last = self._last_sent.get(native)
            if last is not None and now - last < 1.0 / need.rate_hz - 1e-9:
                continue
            self._last_sent[native] = now
            self.sub.on_data(native, Datum(native, value, msg.source_time))

    def _send(self, msg: Message) -> None:
        try:
            name, values = self.mapping.translate_up(self.sub.name, msg.spec_name, msg.values)
        except TransformError as exc:  # all the protection a P2P subsystem has is its own code
            self.errors.append((self.sub.sched.now, msg.spec_name, str(exc)))
            return
        self.uplink_queue.append(Message(name, values, msg.source_time))

    def send_raw(self, name: str, values: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """What faulty subsystem software can do in P2P: put anything on the baseline bus."""
        self.uplink_queue.append(Message(name, values, self.sub.sched.now))

    def _next_uplink(self) -> Message | None:
        return self.uplink_queue.popleft() if self.uplink_queue else None

def diff_interfaces(
    old: BaselineInterface, new: BaselineInterface, renames: Mapping[str, str] | None = None
) -> list[Change]:
    """Changes between two baseline versions. Renames cannot be inferred, so they are given."""
    renames = renames or {}
    changes: list[Change] = []
    old_refs = [f"{m.name}.{e.name}" for m in old.published for e in m.elements]
    new_refs = [f"{m.name}.{e.name}" for m in new.published for e in m.elements]
    for ref in old_refs:
        target = renames.get(ref, ref)
        a, b = old.element(ref), new.element(target)
        if ref in renames:
            changes.append(Change("rename", ref))
        if b is None:
            changes.append(Change("remove", ref))
        elif a is not None:
            ra, rb = a.representation, b.representation
            if ra.units != rb.units:
                changes.append(Change("unit", ref))
            if (ra.encoding, ra.frame) != (rb.encoding, rb.frame):
                changes.append(Change("encoding", ref))
    known = set(old_refs) | set(renames.values())
    changes += [Change("add", ref) for ref in new_refs if ref not in known]
    for spec in old.published:
        other = new.published_message(spec.name)
        if other is not None and other.rate_hz != spec.rate_hz:
            changes.append(Change("rate", spec.name))
    return changes

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    rows = []
    for t in range(trials):
        n, m = rng.randint(*n_range), rng.randint(*m_range)
        density = rng.uniform(*density_range)
        edges, changes = random_scenario(rng, n, m, density, rng.randint(*changes_range))
        p2p, br = impact_p2p(changes, edges), impact_bridge(changes, edges)
        rows.append(
            {
                "trial": t,
                "n": n,
                "m": m,
                "density": round(density, 3),
                "changes": len(changes),
                **{f"p2p_{k}": v for k, v in vars(p2p).items()},
                **{f"bridge_{k}": v for k, v in vars(br).items()},
            }
        )
    return rows

def run_scenario(scenario: Scenario, world: ModuleType) -> tuple[System, int]:
    """Build the system, schedule the events and run it. Returns the system and the version."""
    version = scenario.version if scenario.version is not None else world.VERSIONS[0]
    if version not in world.VERSIONS:
        raise ScenarioError(
            f"{scenario.name}: the {scenario.example} example has baseline versions {list(world.VERSIONS)}, not {version}"
        )
    system = world.build(version, scenario.seed, **scenario.bridge)
    assert system.bridge is not None
    for i, event in enumerate(scenario.events):
        at = float(event["at"])
        if "stall" in event:
            system.bridge.stall(at, float(event["stall"]))
            continue
        send = event["send"]
        sender = system.subsystems.get(send["from"])
        if sender is None:
            raise ScenarioError(
                f"{scenario.name}: events[{i}].send.from {send['from']!r} is not a subsystem; "
                f"choose from {sorted(system.subsystems)}"
            )
        system.sched.at(
            at,
            lambda s=sender, m=send["message"], v=dict(send["values"]): s.send(m, v),
        )
    system.run(scenario.duration_s)
    return system, version

def findings(summary: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    """What happened in a run, in plain sentences, for people who do not read tables."""
    out = []
    for name, s in summary["subsystems"].items():
        text = f"{name} received {s['received']} items"
        if s["mean_age_ms"] is not None:
            text += f", on average {s['mean_age_ms']:.1f} ms old when they arrived"
        if s["time_avg_age_ms"] is not None:
            text += (
                f". Counting the time it held each one, its data was on average {s['time_avg_age_ms']:.1f} ms old"
                f" and at worst {s['peak_age_ms']:.1f} ms old"
            )
        extras = []
        if s["stale_input"]:
            extras.append(
                f"its {s['stale_input']} data was older than it tolerates for {s['stale_s']:.2f} s of the run"
            )
        if s["estimated"]:
            extras.append(f"{s['estimated']} of them were estimates, not real samples")
        if s["late"]:
            extras.append(f"{s['late']} arrived later than its latency budget allows")
        if s["unavailable"]:
            extras.append(
                "it was told these inputs are no longer available: " + ", ".join(s["unavailable"])
            )
        if s["issues"]:
            extras.append("it reports: " + "; ".join(s["issues"]))
        out.append(
            text + (". " + "; ".join(extras).capitalize() if extras else ", with no problems") + "."
        )
    b = summary.get("bridge")
    if b:
        counts = b["event_counts"]
        health = sorted(
            k.split(".", 1)[1]
            for k in counts
            if k.startswith("health.") and k != "health.recovered"
        )
        if counts.get("bridge.stall"):
            out.append(
                "The Bridge stalled and then resumed. The health monitor reported: "
                + (", ".join(health) or "nothing")
                + ". Data held through the stall arrives with its original, older time, so the receivers can see how old it is."
            )
        elif health:
            out.append("The health monitor reported: " + ", ".join(health) + ".")
        if b["blocked_by_cyber_monitor"]:
            out.append(
                f"The cyber monitor blocked {b['blocked_by_cyber_monitor']} message(s) that were not allowed to cross."
            )
        if b["rejected_by_translator"]:
            out.append(
                f"The Translator Module rejected {b['rejected_by_translator']} message(s) with bad or out-of-range values."
            )
        if b["estimates_delivered"]:
            out.append(
                f"{b['estimates_delivered']} estimated samples were delivered to fill gaps; they are marked as estimates and are as old as the real sample they are based on."
            )
    p = summary["platform"]
    out.append(
        f"The baseline accepted {p['accepted']} request(s) and rejected {len(p['rejected'])}."
        + (" Nothing bad reached it." if b and not p["rejected"] else "")
    )
    n = summary["network"]
    out.append(
        "No unique system has a link that skips the Bridge."
        if not n["bypass_links"]
        else f"{n['bypass_links']} link(s) skip the Bridge."
    )
    return out

    n = summary["network"]
    lines.append(f"Links that skip the Bridge: {n['bypass_links']}")

def summarize(system: System) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Counts, ages and issues for every subsystem, plus Bridge, baseline and network state."""
    subsystems: dict[str, Any] = {}
    end = system.sched.now
    for name, sub in system.subsystems.items():
        ages = [r.age for r in sub.received]
        profiles = list(_age_profiles(sub, end).items())
        worst = max(profiles, key=lambda p: p[1][2], default=None)
        subsystems[name] = {
            "protocol": sub.protocol,
            "inputs": len(sub.needs),
            "received": len(sub.received),
            "estimated": sum(1 for r in sub.received if r.datum.estimated),
            "mean_age_ms": _ms(sum(ages) / len(ages)) if ages else None,
            "max_age_ms": _ms(max(ages)) if ages else None,
            "time_avg_age_ms": _ms(sum(p[1][0] for p in profiles) / len(profiles))
            if profiles
            else None,
            "peak_age_ms": _ms(max(p[1][1] for p in profiles)) if profiles else None,
            "stale_s": round(worst[1][2], 6) if worst else 0.0,
            "stale_input": worst[0] if worst and worst[1][2] > 0 else None,
            "late": len(sub.late),
            "issues": sub.check(),
            "unavailable": dict(sub.unavailable),
            "annunciations": [
                {"time_s": round(t, 6), "kind": kind, "detail": detail}
                for t, kind, detail in sub.annunciations
            ],
        }
    out: dict[str, Any] = {"time_s": round(system.sched.now, 6), "subsystems": subsystems}
    bridge = system.bridge
    if bridge is not None:
        kinds: dict[str, int] = {}
        for e in bridge.log.events:
            kinds[e.kind] = kinds.get(e.kind, 0) + 1
        out["bridge"] = {
            "identity_paths_used": bridge.tm.identity_count,
            "translated_paths_used": bridge.tm.translated_count,
            "decimated": bridge.uid.decimated,
            "estimates_delivered": bridge.uid.estimates,
            "blocked_by_cyber_monitor": bridge.cyber.blocked,
            "rejected_by_translator": bridge.tm.rejected,
            "oiu_rejected_in": bridge.oiu.rejected_in,
            "oiu_rejected_out": bridge.oiu.rejected_out,
            "event_counts": dict(sorted(kinds.items())),
            "events": [
                {"time_s": round(e.time, 6), "source": e.source, "kind": e.kind, "detail": e.detail}
                for e in bridge.log.events
            ],
        }
    platform = system.platform
    out["platform"] = {
        "accepted": len(platform.accepted),
        "rejected": [{"time_s": round(t, 6), "reason": why} for t, why in platform.rejected],
        "emitted": dict(platform.emitted),
    }
    out["network"] = {
        "links": len(system.network.links),
        "bypass_links": len(system.network.bypass_links()),
        "problems": system.network.problems(),
    }
    return out

def describe(world: ModuleType, version: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The baseline interface, the subsystems, and every path between them, for one version."""
    dic = world.dictionary(version)
    spec = yaml.safe_load(spec_path(world, version).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    mapping = load_module(generated_path(world, version))
    identity = {(ref, f"{sub}.{native}"): ident for ref, sub, native, ident in mapping.DOWNLINKS}

    def rep(r: Any) -> str:
        return f"{r.encoding}, {r.units}, {r.frame}"

    paths = []
    for entry in spec.get("downlinks", []):
        removed = entry.get("status") == "removed"
        transforms = [_transform_label(t) for t in entry.get("transforms", [])]
        paths.append(
            {
                "from": entry["from"],
                "to": entry["to"],
                "kind": "removed"
                if removed
                else ("identity" if identity[(entry["from"], entry["to"])] else "converted"),
                "transforms": transforms,
                "reason": entry.get("reason", "") if removed else "",
            }
        )
    return {
        "example": world.NAME,
        "version": version,
        "baseline": {
            "published": [
                {
                    "message": m.name,
                    "rate_hz": m.rate_hz,
                    "elements": [
                        {"name": e.name, "representation": rep(e.representation)}
                        for e in m.elements
                    ],
                }
                for m in dic.interface.published
            ],
            "accepted": [m.name for m in dic.interface.accepted],
        },
        "subsystems": [
            {
                "name": name,
                "protocol": next((n.representation.protocol for n in needs), "n/a"),
                "inputs": [
                    {
                        "name": n.native_name,
                        "representation": rep(n.representation),
                        "max_rate_hz": n.rate_hz,
                        "latency_budget_ms": round(1000 * n.latency_budget_s, 3),

                    for n in needs
                ],
                "outputs": [o.message_name for o in dic.outputs.get(name, ())],
            }
            for name, needs in dic.needs.items()
        ],
        "paths": paths,
        "uplinks": [
            {
                "from": u["from"],

    def _allowed_hosts(self) -> set[str]:
        return {f"127.0.0.1:{self.port}", f"localhost:{self.port}"}

    def _store(self, files: dict[str, tuple[str, bytes]]) -> str:
        run_id = secrets.token_urlsafe(9)
        self._results[run_id] = files
        while len(self._results) > KEEP_RESULTS:
            self._results.popitem(last=False)
        return run_id

    def handle(
        self, method: str, target: str, headers: Mapping[str, str], body: bytes = b""
    ) -> Response:
        if headers.get("Host", "") not in self._allowed_hosts():
            return self._plain(403, "Unexpected Host header. Open the address printed by the app.")
        url = urlsplit(target)
        query = parse_qs(url.query, keep_blank_values=True)
        try:
            if method == "GET":
                return self._get(url.path, query)
            if method == "POST":
                if len(body) > MAX_BODY:
                    return self._plain(413, "That request is too large.")
                form = parse_qs(body.decode("utf-8", "replace"), keep_blank_values=True)
                if not hmac.compare_digest(_first(form, "t"), self.token):
                    return self._plain(
                        403, "This page has expired. Go back, reload it and try again."
                    )
                return self._post(url.path, form)
        except ScenarioError as exc:
            return self._page("Something to fix", self._error_html(str(exc)), "/", status=200)
        except FileNotFoundError as exc:
            message = (
                "The example files were not found. Run the app from a clone of the repository, "
                f"or set BRIDGE_ISLAND_EXAMPLES. ({exc})"
            )
            return self._page("Examples not found", self._error_html(message), "/", status=200)
        except Exception:  # last line of defence: one bad request must not take the app down
            traceback.print_exc()
            message = "Something went wrong inside the app. The details are in the black window."
            return self._page("Something went wrong", self._error_html(message), "/", status=500)
        return self._plain(405, "Method not allowed.")

    @staticmethod
    def _plain(status: int, text: str) -> Response:
        return Response(status, text.encode("utf-8"), "text/plain; charset=utf-8")

    @staticmethod
    def _error_html(message: str) -> str:
        return (
            f'<div class="error" role="alert"><strong>Please check this:</strong> {E(message)}</div>'
            '<p>Use your browser\'s Back button to change it, or <a href="/">start again</a>.</p>'
        )

    def _page(self, title: str, body: str, active: str, status: int = 200) -> Response:
        nav = "".join(
            f'<a href="{href}"{" aria-current=page" if href == active else ""}>{E(label)}</a>'
            for href, label in NAV

        doc = (
            '<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8">'
            '<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">'
            f"<title>{E(title)} - bridge-island</title><style>{REPORT_CSS}{DASHBOARD_CSS}{EXTRA_CSS}</style></head><body>"
            '<a class="skip" href="#main">Skip to content</a>'
            f'<header class="appbar"><div><strong>bridge-island</strong><span class="ver">{bridge_island.__version__}</span>'
            f'<span class="note">{E(NOTE)}</span></div></header>'
            f'<nav class="tabs" aria-label="Main"><div>{nav}</div></nav><main id="main">{body}'
            "</main></body></html>"

    # ---- routing -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _get(self, path: str, query: Mapping[str, list[str]]) -> Response:
        if path == "/":
            return self._page("Run a simulation", self._home(query), "/")
        if path == "/scenarios":
            return self._page("Scenario files", self._scenarios_page(), "/scenarios")
        if path == "/report":
            return self._page("Full report", self._report_form(query), "/report")
        if path == "/rules":
            return self._page("Check the guidelines", self._rules_form(), "/rules")
        if path == "/experiments":
            return self._page("Experiments", self._experiments_form(), "/experiments")
        if path == "/help":
            return self._page("Help", self._help(), "/help")
        if path.startswith("/download/"):
            return self._download(path)
        return self._page(
            "Not found", '<h1>Page not found</h1><p><a href="/">Back to the start</a></p>', "", 404
        )

    def _post(self, path: str, form: Mapping[str, list[str]]) -> Response:
        if path == "/run":
            return self._run_quick(form)
        if path == "/run-scenario":
            return self._run_scenario_form(form)
        if path == "/report":
            return self._report(form)
        if path == "/rules":
            return self._rules(form)
        if path == "/experiments":
            return self._experiment(form)
        return self._plain(404, "Not found.")

    def _download(self, path: str) -> Response:
        parts = unquote(path).split("/")
        if len(parts) != 4 or parts[1] != "download":
            return self._plain(404, "Not found.")
        files = self._results.get(parts[2])
        entry = files.get(parts[3]) if files else None
        if entry is None:
            return self._plain(404, "That result is no longer available. Run it again.")
        content_type, data = entry
        return Response(
            200, data, content_type, {"Content-Disposition": f'attachment; filename="{parts[3]}"'}
        )

    def _scenario_dict(self, form: Mapping[str, list[str]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        example = _first(form, "example", "aviation")
        if example not in EXAMPLES:
            raise ScenarioError(f"Choose one of the examples: {', '.join(EXAMPLES)}")

        duration = _num(form, "duration", 8.0, 1.0, MAX_DURATION_S, "How long")
        seed = int(_num(form, "seed", 1, -(10**9), 10**9, "Random seed"))
        events: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        if _first(form, "stall"):

            events.append(
                {"at": at, "stall": _num(form, "stall_for", 1.5, 0.1, duration, "Stall length")}
            )
        fault = _first(form, "fault", "none")
        if fault != "none":
            catalogue = fault_messages(
                world, version if version in world.VERSIONS else world.VERSIONS[0]
            )
            if fault not in catalogue:
                raise ScenarioError("Choose one of the listed faulty messages.")
            _, message, values = catalogue[fault]
            events.append(
                {
                    "at": _num(form, "fault_at", 2.0, 0, duration, "Faulty message time"),
                    "send": {
                        "from": world.CONTAINMENT["sender"],
                        "message": message,
                        "values": values,
                    },
                }
            )
        data: dict[str, Any] = {
            "name": "from_the_app",
            "example": example,
            "version": version,
            "seed": seed,
            "duration_s": duration,
            "bridge": {
                "time_tag": _first(form, "time_tag", "source"),
                "rate_policy": _first(form, "rate_policy", "cap"),
            },
        }
        if events:
            data["events"] = events
        return data

    def _simulate(self, data: Any, source: str) -> tuple[Scenario, System, ModuleType, int]:
        scenario = (
            parse_scenario_text(data, source)
            if isinstance(data, str)
            else parse_scenario(data, source)
        )
        world = load_world(scenario.example)
        with self._lock:
            system, version = run_scenario(scenario, world)
        return scenario, system, world, version

            raise ScenarioError(f"Choose one of the examples: {', '.join(EXAMPLES)}")
        seed = int(_num(form, "seed", 1, -(10**9), 10**9, "Random seed"))
        trials = int(_num(form, "trials", 300, 10, MAX_TRIALS, "Random trials"))
        buffer = io.StringIO()
        with self._lock, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp, contextlib.redirect_stdout(buffer):
            files = experiments.run(name, load_world(example), seed, Path(tmp), trials)
            stored: dict[str, tuple[str, bytes]] = {}
            images = []
            for path in files.values():
                data = path.read_bytes()
                if path.suffix == ".png":
                    images.append(
                        f'<img class="plot" alt="{E(path.stem.replace("_", " "))} (synthetic, illustrative)" src="data:image/png;base64,{base64.b64encode(data).decode()}">'
                    )
                stored[path.name] = (
                    "image/png" if path.suffix == ".png" else "text/csv; charset=utf-8",
                    data,
                )
        run_id = self._store(stored)
        links = "".join(
            f'<a class="button secondary" href="/download/{run_id}/{E(n)}">{E(n)}</a>'
            for n in stored
        )
        text = "\n".join(
            line for line in buffer.getvalue().splitlines() if not line.startswith("wrote ")
        )
        title = EXPERIMENTS[name][0]
        body = (
            f'<h1>{E(title)}: {E(example)}</h1><p class="banner">{E(NOTE)} Seed {seed}.</p>'
            f"<pre>{E(text)}</pre>{''.join(images)}<h2>Files</h2><p>{links}</p>"
            '<p><a class="button secondary" href="/experiments">Run another</a></p>'
        )
        return self._page(title, body, "/experiments")

    # ---- help ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _help(self) -> str:
        terms = "".join(f"<dt>{E(t)}</dt><dd>{E(d)}</dd>" for t, d in HELP_TERMS)
        return f"""<h1>Help</h1>
<h2>What is this?</h2>
<p>A simulation that shows an integration pattern: a host platform that you cannot change (the Baseline Island), your own
systems (the Unique Island), and one layer between them (the Bridge). You can change what happens during a run and see what the
Bridge does about it. {E(NOTE)} It is not flight or medical software and is not certified.</p>
<h2>Where do I start?</h2>
<ol><li>On <a href="/">Run a simulation</a>, press <em>Run</em> with the defaults, then try a quick start such as
<em>The Bridge stalls for 1.5 s</em>.</li>
<li>Read <em>What happened</em> at the top of the result.</li>
<li>Try <a href="/rules">Check the guidelines</a> and the <a href="/report">Full report</a>.</li></ol>
<h2>Reading the charts</h2>
<p>Each chart shows one system. Across: when the data was delivered. Up: how old the data was when it arrived. A dot far
above the others is old data. Different systems use different marker shapes, and hollow markers are estimates, so colour is
never the only clue.</p>
<h2>Scenario files</h2>
<p>A scenario is a short text file in YAML. Example:</p>
<pre>name: my_run

version: 1              # baseline version

  time_tag: source      # source (correct) or delivery (the error)
  rate_policy: cap      # cap or extrapolate

<h2>Words used</h2><dl>{terms}</dl>
